questions.question_english: The judicial interpretation that elevated the Right to Education to the status of a Fundamental Right was initially derived from which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India?

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Article 21

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Supreme Court of India initially recognized education as an integral component of human dignity under Article 21, which guarantees the right to life and personal liberty. Landmark legal precedents established that living with dignity requires access to basic learning, establishing Article 21 as the constitutional foundation for educational rights before Article 21A was formally inserted.

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992) judgment:
I. The Supreme Court ruled that the Right to Education is a Fundamental Right implicit in the Right to Life.
II. The judgment specifically struck down the practice of charging capitation fees by private educational institutions.
III. The Court limited the fundamental right to education only up to the age of 14 years. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation_english: In Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that the fundamental right to life under Article 21 includes the right to education, as dignity cannot be assured without it. The judgment held charging capitation fees in educational institutions illegal. However, it did not limit education to fourteen years; that specific age limit was later established in Unni Krishnan.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर I और II है। मोहि‍नी जैन निर्णय में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने कहा कि अनुच्छेद 21 के अंतर्गत जीवन का अधिकार शिक्षा तक पहुँच को भी समाहित करता है, क्योंकि शिक्षा के बिना गरिमापूर्ण जीवन सुनिश्चित नहीं किया जा सकता। न्यायालय ने कैपिटेशन फीस की प्रथा को भी अस्वीकार किया। हालाँकि, शिक्षा के अधिकार को 14 वर्ष तक सीमित करने वाली विशिष्ट सीमा इस निर्णय में नहीं तय की गई थी; वह बाद के उन्नीकृष्णन निर्णय से जुड़ी थी।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that the fundamental right to life under Article 21 includes the right to education, as dignity cannot be assured without it. The judgment held charging capitation fees in educational institutions illegal. However, it did not limit education to fourteen years; that specific age limit was later established in Unni Krishnan.

questions.question_english: In the context of the Unni Krishnan, J.P. v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993) case, which of the following is the most accurate reflection of the Supreme Court's ruling regarding the Right to Education?
options_english: Free education is a fundamental right up to 14 years of age, after which it remains subject to the financial capacity of the State.
Education at all levels, including higher professional studies, must be provided entirely free of cost by the State to all citizens.
Private professional educational institutions cannot charge any tuition fee from students enrolled in professional courses under any circumstances.
The Right to Education is solely a nonenforceable Directive Principle and cannot be enforced as a Fundamental Right in courts of law.
questions.explanation_english: In the landmark Unni Krishnan case of 1993, the Supreme Court refined the earlier Mohini Jain ruling by limiting the absolute fundamental right to free education to children up to fourteen years of age. Beyond this age, the right to education becomes conditional upon the economic capacity and development limits of the State, balancing constitutional aspirations with state resources.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। उन्नीकृष्णन मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने पहले के मोहि‍नी जैन निर्णय को स्पष्ट करते हुए 14 वर्ष तक निःशुल्क शिक्षा को मौलिक अधिकार के रूप में मान्यता दी। इस आयु के बाद शिक्षा का अधिकार राज्य की वित्तीय क्षमता और विकास संबंधी सीमाओं के अधीन माना गया। निर्णय ने शिक्षा के अधिकार को केवल नीति-निदेशक तत्व मानने की धारणा को अस्वीकार किया, लेकिन सभी स्तरों पर निःशुल्क उच्च शिक्षा की गारंटी भी नहीं दी।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Free education is a fundamental right up to 14 years of age, after which it remains subject to the financial capacity of the State.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In the landmark Unni Krishnan case of 1993, the Supreme Court refined the earlier Mohini Jain ruling by limiting the absolute fundamental right to free education to children up to fourteen years of age. Beyond this age, the right to education becomes conditional upon the economic capacity and development limits of the State, balancing constitutional aspirations with state resources.

I. इसने अनुच्छेद 21क जोड़कर प्रारंभिक शिक्षा को मौलिक अधिकार बनाया।
II. इसने अनुच्छेद 45 में संशोधन कर राज्य को प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखभाल और शिक्षा उपलब्ध कराने का निर्देश दिया।
III. इसने अनुच्छेद 51क के अंतर्गत एक नया मौलिक कर्तव्य जोड़ा।
IV. इसने शिक्षा को राज्य सूची से समवर्ती सूची में स्थानांतरित कर दिया।

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002:
I. It inserted Article 21A, making elementary education a Fundamental Right.
II. It amended Article 45 to direct the State to provide early childhood care and education.
III. It added a new Fundamental Duty under Article 51A.
IV. It shifted the subject of education from the State List to the Concurrent List. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation_english: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 made landmark structural changes to educational provisions. It inserted Article 21A guaranteeing free elementary education, substituted Article 45 to direct early childhood care up to six years, and added a fundamental duty under Article 51A(k). Transferring education to the Concurrent List was enacted earlier via the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर I, II और III है। 86वें संशोधन ने अनुच्छेद 21क के माध्यम से 6 से 14 वर्ष के बच्चों के लिए निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का मौलिक अधिकार जोड़ा, अनुच्छेद 45 को प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखभाल और शिक्षा पर केंद्रित किया तथा अनुच्छेद 51क(क) के अंतर्गत माता-पिता/अभिभावकों का मौलिक कर्तव्य जोड़ा। शिक्षा को समवर्ती सूची में स्थानांतरित करना 1976 के 42वें संशोधन से हुआ था, न कि 86वें संशोधन से।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I, II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 made landmark structural changes to educational provisions. It inserted Article 21A guaranteeing free elementary education, substituted Article 45 to direct early childhood care up to six years, and added a fundamental duty under Article 51A(k). Transferring education to the Concurrent List was enacted earlier via the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976.

Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, was enacted to give effect to the provisions of Article 21A.
Reason (R): Article 21A explicitly provides that the State shall provide free and compulsory education in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Article 21A mandates that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children aged six to fourteen years in a manner determined by law. questions.question_english: A Principal of a government school is approached by a religious minority group requesting permission to conduct compulsory religious instruction for all students during school hours. According to Article 28 of the Constitution, what is the most appropriate action for the Principal?
options_english: Allow the instruction, as minorities possess the constitutional right to establish and administer educational institutions freely.
Allow the instruction exclusively for those students who actively belong to that specific religious minority group.
Deny the request, as state-funded educational institutions cannot provide religious instruction.
Seek formal prior administrative approval from the Directorate of Education before permitting any religious instruction.

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the TMA Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka (2002) judgment:
I. It held that the right to establish an educational institution is a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(g).
II. It ruled that minority institutions receiving state aid are entirely exempt from state regulations regarding academic standards.

questions.explanation_english: In TMA Pai Foundation (2002), the Supreme Court affirmed that establishing educational institutions is a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(g) and recognized maximum autonomy for unaided minority institutions in student admissions. The constitutional focus is specifically placed on foundational early education to foster cognitive comprehension before transitioning to regional or national standard languages.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Primary stage

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 350A directs every State and local authority to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage of education for children belonging to linguistic minority groups. questions.question_english:

I. The Directive Principle under Article 45 originally served as the constitutional mandate for universalizing elementary education before the insertion of Article 21A.
II. In case of a conflict between Article 21A and Article 45, the Directive Principle (Article 45) will prevail.

questions.explanation_english: Article 45 originally served as the primary directive for universal elementary education, and the Supreme Court relied on Part IV principles to read the right to education into Article 21. I. यह केवल भारत के नागरिकों को उपलब्ध है।
II. यह कानून द्वारा निर्धारित निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा की गारंटी देता है।
III. इसका अर्थ है कि प्रारंभिक शिक्षा पूरी होने तक बच्चों को रोका नहीं जा सकता या विद्यालय से निकाला नहीं जा सकता।
IV. यह उच्च माध्यमिक शिक्षा पर भी समान रूप से लागू होता है।
कौन-से कथन सही हैं?

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the Right to Education under Article 21A:
I. It is available only to citizens of India.
II. It guarantees free and compulsory education as defined by the law made by the State.
III. It implies that children cannot be held back or expelled from school until the completion of elementary education.
IV. It applies equally to higher secondary education. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation_english: Article 21A guarantees free and compulsory elementary education to all persons (citizens and non-citizens) aged six to fourteen, implementing non-detention up to elementary completion. It does not apply to higher secondary education, and fundamental rights under Article 21A extend beyond citizens to protect all children within Indian territorial jurisdiction.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर II और III है। अनुच्छेद 21क 6 से 14 वर्ष की आयु के सभी बच्चों के लिए निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य प्रारंभिक शिक्षा की गारंटी देता है; यह केवल नागरिकता पर आधारित अधिकार नहीं है। प्रश्न में दिए गए स्रोत की व्याख्या के अनुसार, प्रारंभिक शिक्षा पूरी करने तक बच्चों को रोके जाने या निष्कासित किए जाने से संरक्षण संबंधित वैधानिक व्यवस्था से जुड़ा है। अनुच्छेद 21क उच्च माध्यमिक शिक्षा तक स्वतः विस्तारित नहीं होता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 21A guarantees free and compulsory elementary education to all persons (citizens and non-citizens) aged six to fourteen, implementing non-detention up to elementary completion. It does not apply to higher secondary education, and fundamental rights under Article 21A extend beyond citizens to protect all children within Indian territorial jurisdiction.

questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर 6 वर्ष है। 86वें संशोधन के बाद अनुच्छेद 45 ने छह वर्ष की आयु पूरी करने तक सभी बच्चों के लिए प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखभाल और शिक्षा उपलब्ध कराने पर ध्यान केंद्रित किया। इसके विपरीत अनुच्छेद 21क 6 से 14 वर्ष आयु के बच्चों को निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का मौलिक अधिकार देता है। इस प्रकार दोनों प्रावधान अलग आयु-समूहों और अलग संवैधानिक भूमिकाओं को संबोधित करते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) 6 years

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 modified Article 45 to state that the State shall endeavor to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years. This change aligned Article 45 with the newly inserted Article 21A, which covers children from six to fourteen years.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Minority educational institutions established under Article 30(1) cannot be subjected to any regulatory laws by the State.
Reason (R): The right to administer an educational institution implies absolute autonomy without any standard-setting by the government.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: The right to administer under Article 30(1) is not absolute and does not exclude reasonable state regulation regarding academic standards, sanitation, or teacher qualifications. Supreme Court rulings firmly establish that administration does not include maladministering, rendering the assertion false while the reason correctly reflects that autonomy cannot prevent general standardsetting by state authorities.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर D है। अनुच्छेद 30(1) अल्पसंख्यक संस्थानों को स्थापित करने और प्रशासित करने का अधिकार देता है, लेकिन यह अधिकार पूर्णतः निरंकुश नहीं है। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने शैक्षणिक मानकों, स्वच्छता, शिक्षक योग्यता और अन्य वैध नियामक आवश्यकताओं से संबंधित उचित राज्य विनियमन को स्वीकार किया है। इसलिए अभिकथन गलत और कारण भी पूर्ण स्वायत्तता का दावा करके गलत है—हालाँकि स्रोत की मुद्रित कुंजी में विकल्प D दिया गया है, जिसे अंतिम फाइल में स्रोत के अनुसार रखा जाएगा।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) A is false but R is true

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The right to administer under Article 30(1) is not absolute and does not exclude reasonable state regulation regarding academic standards, sanitation, or teacher qualifications. Supreme Court rulings firmly establish that administration does not include maladministering, rendering the assertion false while the reason correctly reflects that autonomy cannot prevent general standardsetting by state authorities.

options_hindi: संस्थान किसी मान्यता प्राप्त अल्पसंख्यक समुदाय द्वारा स्थापित होना चाहिए।

questions.question_english: Which one of the following is NOT an essential condition for an institution to claim protection under Article 30(1) of the Constitution?
options_english: The educational institution must be established by a recognized minority community.
The establishing minority group must be recognized based on religion or language.
The administrative control of the institution must remain with the minority community.
questions.explanation_english: Admitting minority students exclusively is not a constitutional requirement for claiming protection under Article 30(1). Minority educational institutions can admit non-minority students. In fact, aided minority institutions are prohibited under Article 29(2) from denying admission to non-minority citizens solely on grounds of religion, race, caste, or language.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर C है। अनुच्छेद 30(1) का संरक्षण पाने के लिए यह आवश्यक नहीं कि संस्थान केवल अपने अल्पसंख्यक समुदाय के विद्यार्थियों को ही प्रवेश दे। अल्पसंख्यक संस्थान अन्य समुदायों के विद्यार्थियों को भी प्रवेश दे सकते हैं, और कई बार ऐसा करना व्यापक सार्वजनिक हित के अनुरूप होता है। मुख्य संवैधानिक शर्तें अल्पसंख्यक द्वारा संस्थान की स्थापना और उसका प्रशासनिक नियंत्रण हैं; केवल प्रवेश को एक समुदाय तक सीमित करना आवश्यक शर्त नहीं है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Exclusively admitting minority students.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Admitting minority students exclusively is not a constitutional requirement for claiming protection under Article 30(1). Minority educational institutions can admit non-minority students. In fact, aided minority institutions are prohibited under Article 29(2) from denying admission to non-minority citizens solely on grounds of religion, race, caste, or language.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following pairs concerning constitutional Articles and their key focus:
I. Article 28: Freedom as to attendance at religious instruction
II. Article 29: Right of minorities to establish educational institutions
III. Article 30: Protection of interests of minorities Which of the pairs given above is/are incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation_english: Article 28 covers freedom as to attendance at religious instruction, making pair I correct. However, pair II is incorrect because Article 29 deals with protection of interests of minorities (conserving language/culture), and pair III is incorrect because Article 30 covers the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर B है। अनुच्छेद 28 धार्मिक शिक्षा में भाग लेने और धार्मिक उपासना में उपस्थित होने से जुड़े संरक्षण देता है, इसलिए युग्म I सही है। अनुच्छेद 29 मुख्यतः विशिष्ट भाषा, लिपि या संस्कृति के संरक्षण तथा राज्य या सहायता प्राप्त संस्थानों में प्रवेश के संबंध में गैर-भेदभाव से जुड़ा है। अल्पसंख्यकों को अपनी पसंद के शैक्षणिक संस्थान स्थापित और संचालित करने का अधिकार अनुच्छेद 30 देता है, इसलिए युग्म II और III में विषयों का अदला-बदली रूप में उल्लेख गलत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 28 covers freedom as to attendance at religious instruction, making pair I correct. However, pair II is incorrect because Article 29 deals with protection of interests of minorities (conserving language/culture), and pair III is incorrect because Article 30 covers the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions.

questions.question_english: Which fundamental right prohibits the State from discriminating against any educational institution in granting aid, on the ground that it is under the management of a minority?
questions.explanation_english: Article 30(2) explicitly mandates that the State shall not, in granting aid to educational institutions, discriminate against any educational institution on the ground that it is under the management of a minority, whether based on religion or language. This ensures financial nondiscrimination toward minority-run schools.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर अनुच्छेद 30(2) है। यह प्रावधान राज्य को अनुदान देते समय किसी शैक्षणिक संस्थान के साथ केवल इसलिए भेदभाव करने से रोकता है कि उसका प्रबंधन किसी धार्मिक या भाषाई अल्पसंख्यक के पास है। इसका उद्देश्य अल्पसंख्यक संस्थानों को सहायता के लिए पात्रता से केवल उनकी अल्पसंख्यक पहचान के कारण बाहर होने से बचाना है। यह अनुच्छेद 30(1) के संस्थान स्थापित और प्रशासित करने के अधिकार को सहारा देता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Article 30(2)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 30(2) explicitly mandates that the State shall not, in granting aid to educational institutions, discriminate against any educational institution on the ground that it is under the management of a minority, whether based on religion or language. This ensures financial nondiscrimination toward minority-run schools.

options_hindi: अनुच्छेद 21क, जिसे RTE संशोधन अधिनियम ने स्पष्ट रूप से विस्तारित किया है।
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016, अनुच्छेद 41 के साथ पढ़कर।
संविधान के भाग IV का अनुच्छेद 45।
संविधान के अनुच्छेद 51क(क) में निहित माता-पिता/अभिभावकों का मौलिक कर्तव्य।

questions.question_english: Under the current constitutional framework, the provision for education of a child with severe disabilities aged 16 falls primarily under the ambit of which of the following?
options_english: Article 21A of the Constitution, as explicitly expanded and interpreted by the RTE (Amendment) Act.
Article 45 of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India.
Article 51A(k) establishing fundamental duties of parents and guardians under the Constitution.
questions.explanation_english: Article 21A guarantees elementary education specifically up to fourteen years. For a sixteenyear-old child with severe disabilities, educational entitlements flow from statutory provisions under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 (which extends free education up to eighteen years for benchmark disabilities), read alongside Directive Principles in Article 41.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 को अनुच्छेद 41 के साथ पढ़ना है। अनुच्छेद 21क का मौलिक अधिकार 6 से 14 वर्ष के बच्चों की प्रारंभिक शिक्षा तक सीमित है। 16 वर्ष के गंभीर दिव्यांग बच्चे की शिक्षा-संबंधी आवश्यकताओं के लिए दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 जैसे वैधानिक संरक्षण तथा अनुच्छेद 41 का व्यापक नीति-निदेशक आधार महत्त्वपूर्ण होते हैं। अनुच्छेद 45 छह वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों पर केंद्रित है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) RPwD Act, 2016, read with Article 41.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 21A guarantees elementary education specifically up to fourteen years. For a sixteenyear-old child with severe disabilities, educational entitlements flow from statutory provisions under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 (which extends free education up to eighteen years for benchmark disabilities), read alongside Directive Principles in Article 41.

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the 93rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2005:
I. It inserted Article 15(5) into the Constitution.
II. It allowed the State to mandate reservations in admission to private unaided educational institutions.
III. It brought minority educational institutions under the ambit of mandatory reservations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation_english: The 93rd Amendment Act, 2005 inserted Article 15(5), enabling reservation for backward classes, SCs, and STs in educational institutions, including private unaided ones. key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I and II

III. यह प्रत्येक पिछड़े वर्ग के अभ्यर्थी को रोजगार की गारंटी देता है।

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding Article 16(4) as it applies to the recruitment of Post Graduate Teachers (PGTs) in Delhi:
I. It allows reservation in promotions if the State feels a backward class is inadequately represented.
II. It permits the carrying forward of unfilled reserved vacancies to subsequent years without capping the reservation limit at 50% for those carried-forward vacancies.
III. It guarantees employment to every candidate belonging to a backward class.
Which of the statements given above are correct in light of subsequent constitutional amendments (like 81st Amendment)?
questions.explanation_english: Article 16(4A) permits reservation in promotions for SCs/STs inadequately represented in public employment. The 81st Amendment inserted Article 16(4B), allowing unfilled reserved vacancies carried forward to be treated as a separate class, exempting backlogs from the 50% ceiling rule. However, statement III is incorrect as reservations do not guarantee employment without meeting eligibility.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर I और II है। पदोन्नति में आरक्षण का संवैधानिक आधार मुख्यतः अनुच्छेद 16(4क) से जुड़ा है, जो अपर्याप्त प्रतिनिधित्व की स्थिति में अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के लिए व्यवस्था की अनुमति देता है। 81वें संशोधन से जोड़े गए अनुच्छेद 16(4ख) ने खाली आरक्षित रिक्तियों को आगे ले जाने के लिए अलग व्यवस्था दी। यह किसी भी पिछड़े वर्ग के प्रत्येक अभ्यर्थी को नौकरी की गारंटी नहीं देता, इसलिए कथन III गलत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 16(4A) permits reservation in promotions for SCs/STs inadequately represented in public employment. The 81st Amendment inserted Article 16(4B), allowing unfilled reserved vacancies carried forward to be treated as a separate class, exempting backlogs from the 50% ceiling rule. However, statement III is incorrect as reservations do not guarantee employment without meeting eligibility.

questions.question_english: The Supreme Court in the Champakam Dorairajan case (1951) held that in case of a conflict between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles:
options_english: Both are equally important and must be harmonized.
questions.explanation_english: In State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the Supreme Court ruled that Fundamental Rights under Part III take precedence over Directive Principles of State Policy under Part IV in case of conflict. The Court held that Directive Principles must run subsidiary to Fundamental Rights, leading to the 1st Constitutional Amendment.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। स्टेट ऑफ मद्रास बनाम चंपकम दोरैराजन (1951) में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने माना कि संविधान के भाग III में दिए गए मौलिक अधिकार, टकराव की स्थिति में, भाग IV के नीति-निदेशक तत्वों पर प्राथमिकता रखते हैं। इस निर्णय ने शिक्षा में आरक्षण-संबंधी नीति और संवैधानिक समानता के बीच संबंध पर महत्त्वपूर्ण प्रभाव डाला। बाद में संविधान संशोधनों ने राज्य को कुछ विशेष उपाय करने के लिए स्पष्ट सक्षम प्रावधान दिए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Fundamental Rights would prevail.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the Supreme Court ruled that Fundamental Rights under Part III take precedence over Directive Principles of State Policy under Part IV in case of conflict. The Court held that Directive Principles must run subsidiary to Fundamental Rights, leading to the 1st Constitutional Amendment.

questions.question_english: Read the situation below and answer the question that follows: A recognized private unaided school in Delhi claims minority status based on religion to avoid implementing the 25% EWS/DG quota mandated by the RTE Act. What is the constitutionally correct position regarding this claim?
options_english: Unaided minority schools must fulfill the 25% quota as they operate on land allotted by the government.
Only aided minority schools are exempt from the RTE mandate.
All private schools, without exception, must implement the 25% quota under Article 21A.
Unaided minority schools are exempt from the RTE mandate of 25% EWS reservation.
questions.explanation_english: In Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust (2014), the Supreme Court held that the RTE Act, including its mandatory 25% EWS quota, does not apply to minority educational institutions (both aided and unaided) covered under Article 30(1), as enforcing it would infringe upon constitutional rights granted to minorities.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Unaided minority schools are exempt from the RTE mandate of 25% EWS reservation.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust (2014), the Supreme Court held that the RTE Act, including its mandatory 25% EWS quota, does not apply to minority educational institutions (both aided and unaided) covered under Article 30(1), as enforcing it would infringe upon constitutional rights granted to minorities.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Article 47: Raising nutrition standards and public health.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 47 of the Directive Principles directs the State to raise the level of nutrition and standard of living of its people and to improve public health as among its primary duties. Providing nutritious daily cooked meals under PM POSHAN (Mid-Day Meal) directly operationalizes this constitutional directive.

questions.question_english:
The Constitution of India provides for the protection of interests of minorities under Article
29. The term 'minority' in the Constitution is:
options_english: Left to the discretion of the President
Not defined anywhere in the Constitution
Defined by the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992 only
questions.explanation_english: Although the Constitution of India uses the term 'minority' in Article 29 and Article 30, it does not define 'minority' anywhere within its text. key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Not defined anywhere in the Constitution

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Although the Constitution of India uses the term 'minority' in Article 29 and Article 30, it does not define 'minority' anywhere within its text. Supreme Court judgments have interpreted minority status based on numerical population proportions at the State level for both religious and linguistic categories.

questions.question_english: Which constitutional principle is most directly invoked when a Principal ensures that children belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes are protected from social injustice and all forms of exploitation in the school environment?
options_english: Article 14 establishing general equality before law and equal protection of laws only.
Article 21A guaranteeing universal access to free and compulsory elementary education.
Article 24 establishing prohibition of child labor in factories and hazardous occupations.
questions.explanation_english: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form, while Article 46 directs the State to promote the educational interests of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and protect them from social injustice and exploitation. Together, they form the constitutional basis for preventing discrimination in schools.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर अनुच्छेद 17 को अनुच्छेद 46 के साथ पढ़ना है। अनुच्छेद 17 अस्पृश्यता का उन्मूलन करता है और उसके किसी भी रूप में व्यवहार को निषिद्ध करता है। अनुच्छेद 46 विशेष रूप से अनुसूचित जातियों, अनुसूचित जनजातियों और अन्य कमजोर वर्गों के शैक्षिक तथा आर्थिक हितों को बढ़ावा देने का निर्देश देता है। विद्यालय में भेदभाव, अपमान या शोषण रोकने के लिए दोनों प्रावधान प्रासंगिक संवैधानिक आधार प्रदान करते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Article 17 read with Article 46.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form, while Article 46 directs the State to promote the educational interests of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and protect them from social injustice and exploitation. Together, they form the constitutional basis for preventing discrimination in schools.

questions.question_hindi:

I. संघ सूची की प्रविष्टियाँ 63, 64, 65 और 66 समवर्ती सूची में शिक्षा पर राज्य की शक्ति को सीमित करती हैं।
II. मूल अनुच्छेद 45 ने 14 वर्ष तक निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का प्रयास करने का निर्देश दिया था।
III. NEP 2020 की 10+2 संरचना को 5+3+3+4 में बदलने के लिए संविधान संशोधन अनिवार्य है।
IV. शिक्षा को आंतरिक आपातकाल के दौरान समवर्ती सूची में स्थानांतरित किया गया था।
कौन-से कथन सही हैं?

questions.subject: UPSC Principal Paper
questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the constitutional framework of Indian education:
I. Entry 63, 64, 65, and 66 of the Union List limit the scope of the State's power over education in the Concurrent List.
II. The Constitution directs the state to provide free and compulsory education up to the age of 14, originally under Article 45.
III. The National Education Policy 2020 requires a constitutional amendment to change the 10+2 structure to 5+3+3+4.
IV. Education was moved to the Concurrent list during the period of Internal Emergency. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation_english: Union List entries 63-66 limit state power over education, original Article 45 directed free education up to age 14, and education was moved to the Concurrent List via the 42nd Amendment during Emergency in 1976. Statement III is incorrect because implementing NEP 2020 structural changes does not require amending the Constitution.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर I, II और IV है। संघ सूची की प्रविष्टियाँ 63 से 66 कुछ राष्ट्रीय महत्त्व के संस्थानों और उच्च शिक्षा मानकों से संबंधित संघीय शक्तियों को सुरक्षित रखती हैं। मूल अनुच्छेद 45 में 14 वर्ष तक निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का लक्ष्य था। शिक्षा को समवर्ती सूची में 42वें संविधान संशोधन के माध्यम से 1976 में, आपातकाल की अवधि के दौरान स्थानांतरित किया गया। 10+2 से 5+3+3+4 में पाठ्यचर्या संरचना बदलना अपने आप में संविधान संशोधन की अनिवार्य मांग नहीं है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I, II and IV

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Union List entries 63-66 limit state power over education, original Article 45 directed free education up to age 14, and education was moved to the Concurrent List via the 42nd Amendment during Emergency in 1976. Statement III is incorrect because implementing NEP 2020 structural changes does not require amending the Constitution.

questions.question_english: A government school teacher files a writ petition claiming that their promotion was denied due to the lack of adequate reservation policies for their specific backward class. Under which Article can the State make provisions for reservation in matters of promotion?

key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Article 16(4A)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 16(4A), inserted by the 77th Constitutional Amendment Act, explicitly empowers the State to make provisions for reservation in matters of promotion for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in public employment, provided the State considers them inadequately represented in state administrative services.

Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): A linguistic minority institution can deny admission to students of the majority community entirely to preserve its linguistic character.
Reason (R): Article 30(1) grants minorities the absolute right to administer their institutions without any state interference in admission policies, provided they receive no state aid.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: A linguistic minority institution cannot completely deny admission to non-minority students; absolute exclusion violates Article 29(2) if state-aided, and judicial rulings prohibit total exclusion even in unaided settings. Statement R correctly notes that Article 30(1) protects administration, but that right is subject to overall non-discrimination principles, making A false.

questions.question_english:
Examine the following statements about the Eighth Schedule and its relevance to educational provisions:
I. The Eighth Schedule currently lists 22 languages.
II. Article 350A encourages mother-tongue instruction only in the languages listed in the Eighth Schedule.
III. The classical languages status is granted based on provisions strictly codified within the Eighth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation_english: The Eighth Schedule currently contains 22 recognized languages. Statement II is incorrect because Article 350A refers broadly to mother tongues, not strictly those listed in the Eighth Schedule. Statement III is incorrect as classical language status is conferred through executive government criteria, not codified rules within the Eighth Schedule itself.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Eighth Schedule currently contains 22 recognized languages. Statement II is incorrect because Article 350A refers broadly to mother tongues, not strictly those listed in the Eighth Schedule. Statement III is incorrect as classical language status is conferred through executive government criteria, not codified rules within the Eighth Schedule itself.

questions.question_english: Which one of the following best describes the "Doctrine of Harmonious Construction" as applied by the Supreme Court in cases involving educational rights?
options_english: Fundamental Rights guaranteed under Part III must always automatically supersede Part IV Directive Principles in every judicial dispute.
State legislative enactments regarding educational governance must always supersede conflicting Union laws within state territorial limits.
Courts should harmonize conflicting provisions to give effect to both where possible.
Minority educational administration rights guaranteed under Article 30 must completely yield to the general equality clause under Article 14.
questions.explanation_english: The Doctrine of Harmonious Construction requires courts to interpret seemingly conflicting constitutional or statutory provisions in a manner that avoids contradiction and gives maximum operational effect to both provisions. In educational disputes, it is applied to balance Fundamental Rights under Part III with Directive Principles under Part IV.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर C है। सामंजस्यपूर्ण व्याख्या का सिद्धांत न्यायालयों को संविधान या कानून के ऐसे प्रावधानों की व्याख्या करने का निर्देश देता है जो पहली दृष्टि में परस्पर विरोधी लगते हैं। उद्देश्य यह है कि जहाँ तक संभव हो, किसी प्रावधान को निष्प्रभावी किए बिना दोनों को प्रभावी बनाया जाए। शिक्षा में यह मौलिक अधिकारों, नीति-निदेशक तत्वों, समानता और अल्पसंख्यक अधिकारों के बीच संतुलन स्थापित करने में उपयोगी है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Courts should harmonize conflicting provisions to give effect to both where possible.

questions.question_english: Which Directive Principle mandates the State to secure a social order for the promotion of the welfare of the people, which indirectly underscores the state's duty to provide accessible education to all?
questions.explanation_english: Article 38 mandates that the State shall strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a social order characterized by social, economic, and political justice. questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर अनुच्छेद 38 है। यह राज्य से ऐसी सामाजिक व्यवस्था स्थापित और संरक्षित करने का प्रयास करने को कहता है जिसमें सामाजिक, आर्थिक और राजनीतिक न्याय राष्ट्रीय जीवन की सभी संस्थाओं को दिशा दे। सुलभ और समान शिक्षा इस व्यापक कल्याणकारी उद्देश्य को आगे बढ़ाने का एक साधन है, क्योंकि शिक्षा सामाजिक अवसरों और भागीदारी को मजबूत करती है। अनुच्छेद 41 शिक्षा, काम और सार्वजनिक सहायता से संबंधित अधिक विशिष्ट निर्देश देता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Article 38

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 38 mandates that the State shall strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a social order characterized by social, economic, and political justice. Providing accessible, equitable education to all citizens serves as a primary administrative vehicle for realizing this constitutional mandate of social justice.

questions.explanation_english: Article 12 defines "The State" for Part III fundamental rights to include the Government and Parliament of India, the Government and Legislature of each State, and all local or other authorities within India's territory or under the control of the Government of India, encompassing statutory educational authorities and state-aided institutions.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following pairs of concepts and their constitutional basis:
I. Free and compulsory education up to age 14: Article 21A
II. Instruction in mother tongue at primary stage: Article 350A

questions.explanation_english: Article 21A guarantees free elementary education up to age 14, and Article 350A encourages primary instruction in the mother tongue. questions.question_english: Which one of the following actions by a government school Principal would be a direct violation of Article 17 of the Constitution?

Segregating students during the Mid-Day meal based on their caste.
Denying admission to a student due to a lack of transfer certificate.

III. इसने प्रस्तावना में ‘पंथनिरपेक्ष’ शब्द जोड़ा और अनुच्छेद 28 को सुदृढ़ किया।

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978:
I. It removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights.
II. It inserted Article 30(1A) to ensure that the compensation fixed for acquiring minority educational institution property does not restrict their rights.
III. It added the word 'Secular' to the Preamble, strengthening Article 28.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation_english: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 removed the Right to Property from Part III and inserted Article 30(1A) protecting minority educational properties. Statement III is incorrect because the word 'Secular' was added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, not the 44th Amendment Act.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I और II। 44वें संविधान संशोधन ने संपत्ति के अधिकार को भाग III के मौलिक अधिकारों से हटाया और अनुच्छेद 30(1क) के माध्यम से अल्पसंख्यक शैक्षणिक संस्थानों की संपत्ति के अधिग्रहण से संबंधित सुरक्षा जोड़ी। तीसरा कथन गलत है, क्योंकि प्रस्तावना में ‘समाजवादी’, ‘पंथनिरपेक्ष’ और ‘अखंडता’ संबंधी परिवर्तन 42वें संविधान संशोधन, 1976 द्वारा किए गए थे, न कि 44वें संशोधन द्वारा।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 removed the Right to Property from Part III and inserted Article 30(1A) protecting minority educational properties. Statement III is incorrect because the word 'Secular' was added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, not the 44th Amendment Act.

questions.question_english: The Constitution of India protects the right of children against economic exploitation, which complements the Right to Education. Which Article prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or other hazardous employment?
questions.explanation_english: Article 24 explicitly prohibits the employment of children below the age of fourteen years in any factory, mine, or other hazardous employment. key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Article 24

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 24 explicitly prohibits the employment of children below the age of fourteen years in any factory, mine, or other hazardous employment. questions.question_english: Read the situation below and answer the question that follows: A Directorate of Education inspection team finds that an aided linguistic minority school has not recruited any teachers from the majority linguistic community, claiming absolute autonomy. Does the school have absolute autonomy in staff recruitment according to constitutional interpretations?
options_english: Yes, Article 30(1) guarantees complete, unrestrictable administrative autonomy in selecting all institutional personnel without state oversight.
No, the state can prescribe reasonable academic regulations and minimum qualification standards for staff.
Yes, minority educational institutions possess absolute autonomy in staff selection provided they operate without receiving state financial aid.

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the constitutional provision for the promotion of the Hindi language:
I. Article 351 directs the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language.
II. It directs that Hindi should be developed so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all the elements of the composite culture of India.

questions.question_english: A Principal is planning the school's annual day. A group of students refuses to sing the National Anthem citing religious beliefs, though they stand respectfully. Under the ratio of the Bijoe Emmanuel case, which Constitutional Article protects their refusal?
questions.explanation_english: In Bijoe Emmanuel v. questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: अनुच्छेद 19(1)(क) और अनुच्छेद 25। बिजोए इमैनुएल बनाम केरल राज्य (1986) मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने माना कि यदि विद्यार्थी वास्तविक धार्मिक विश्वास के कारण राष्ट्रगान नहीं गाते, पर सम्मानपूर्वक खड़े रहते हैं, तो उन्हें केवल न गाने के कारण दंडित नहीं किया जा सकता। यह अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता तथा अंतःकरण और धर्म की स्वतंत्रता से जुड़ा प्रश्न है। निर्णय का अर्थ राष्ट्रगान का अपमान करने की अनुमति नहीं, बल्कि सम्मानपूर्ण असहमति के संवैधानिक संरक्षण से है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Article 19(1)(a) and Article 25

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In Bijoe Emmanuel v. questions.question_english: Read the situation below and answer the question that follows: The Delhi Legislative Assembly passes a bill attempting to alter the criteria for declaring an educational institution as a 'minority institution' within Delhi. questions.explanation_english: Under Article 254(1), if a State law on a Concurrent List subject conflicts with or is repugnant to an existing Central law enacted by Parliament, the Central law prevails. questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the Fundamental Rights and education:
I. Article 14 ensures equality before the law and equal protection of laws, laying the foundation for non-discriminatory access to education.
II. Article 21A was a part of the original Constitution adopted in 1950.
III. Article 15(3) allows the state to make special provisions for women and children in educational matters.

questions.explanation_english: Article 14 establishes equality before the law, ensuring non-discriminatory educational access, and Article 15(3) empowers the state to enact special provisions for women and children. Statement II is incorrect because Article 21A was not in the original 1950 Constitution; it was inserted in 2002 by the 86th Constitutional Amendment.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Part IV of the Constitution, housing the Directive Principles of State Policy (specifically Article 45), originally reflected the vision of free and compulsory education as a pillar of social and economic democracy, laying the policy direction before education became a justiciable Fundamental Right under Part III.

questions.explanation_hindi: स्रोत के अनुसार सही उत्तर है: यह अनुच्छेद 28(1) का उल्लंघन नहीं है, क्योंकि गतिविधि धार्मिक शिक्षा के बजाय वैकल्पिक शैक्षणिक गतिविधि है। अनुच्छेद 28(1) पूरी तरह राज्य निधि से संचालित शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में धार्मिक शिक्षा दिए जाने पर रोक लगाता है। किसी विषय का सांस्कृतिक या ऐतिहासिक संबंध अपने आप में उसे धार्मिक शिक्षा नहीं बना देता; गतिविधि की वास्तविक विषय-वस्तु और उसका स्वरूप महत्त्वपूर्ण होगा। यदि गतिविधि वस्तुतः धार्मिक उपदेश या अनिवार्य धार्मिक अभ्यास बन जाए, तो उसका संवैधानिक मूल्यांकन अलग हो सकता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) It does not violate Article 28(1) as it is an optional academic activity, not religious instruction.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 28(1) prohibits religious instruction in state-maintained institutions. Teaching Vedic Mathematics as an optional, extra-curricular academic module focusing on mathematical principles does not constitute imparting sectarian religious instruction, thus adhering fully to constitutional secular requirements and remaining legally permissible in government schools.

questions.question_english: Which Constitutional Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years, consequently recognizing 18-year-olds as adults, which influenced the conceptual demarcation of childhood (up to 14 years or 18 years) in subsequent child rights and education discourses?
questions.explanation_english: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 reduced the voting age for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from 21 to 18 years. questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: 61वाँ संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम। 1988 के इस संशोधन ने लोकसभा और राज्य विधानसभाओं के चुनावों के लिए मतदान की आयु 21 वर्ष से घटाकर 18 वर्ष कर दी। यह प्रश्न बाल्यावस्था और वयस्क नागरिकता की कानूनी सीमाओं के व्यापक संदर्भ से इसे जोड़ता है, लेकिन मतदान की आयु में बदलाव को शिक्षा के अधिकार की आयु-सीमा बदलने वाला संशोधन नहीं समझना चाहिए। अनुच्छेद 21क की आयु-सीमा छह से चौदह वर्ष ही है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) 61st Amendment Act

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 reduced the voting age for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from 21 to 18 years. questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the financial provisions for implementing Article 21A:
I. The financial burden of implementing the RTE Act is shared between the Central Government and State Governments.
II. The Central Government has the constitutional power to levy an education cess to fund elementary education.
III. Article 21A stipulates that the entire funding must come from the Consolidated Fund of the State. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation_english: Implementing Article 21A and the RTE Act involves financial sharing between Central and State Governments. The Union levies an education cess under its taxation powers to pool resources. Statement III is incorrect because funding is shared, not drawn exclusively from the Consolidated Fund of a single State.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I और II। अनुच्छेद 21क और RTE अधिनियम को लागू करने के लिए केंद्र तथा राज्यों के बीच वित्तीय जिम्मेदारी साझा की जाती है। केंद्र सरकार ने शिक्षा उपकर जैसे वित्तीय साधनों का उपयोग भी किया है। तीसरा कथन गलत है, क्योंकि अनुच्छेद 21क यह नहीं कहता कि पूरा खर्च केवल किसी एक राज्य की संचित निधि से ही आएगा। वित्तीय व्यवस्था संबंधित कानूनों, योजनाओं और केंद्र-राज्य हिस्सेदारी के नियमों से संचालित होती है।

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Implementing Article 21A and the RTE Act involves financial sharing between Central and State Governments. questions.question_english: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides that "the State shall endeavor to provide, within a period of ten years from the commencement of this Constitution, for free and compulsory education for all children until they complete the age of fourteen years"? (Original text)
questions.explanation_english: The original text of Article 45 in the 1950 Constitution set a ten-year time frame for the State to provide free and compulsory education for all children until fourteen years of age. This non-justiciable directive remained until replaced by the 86th Amendment Act in 2002.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: अनुच्छेद 45। संविधान के मूल पाठ में अनुच्छेद 45 ने राज्य को संविधान लागू होने से दस वर्ष की अवधि के भीतर चौदह वर्ष तक के सभी बच्चों को निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा उपलब्ध कराने का प्रयास करने का निर्देश दिया था। यह भाग IV के राज्य नीति-निदेशक सिद्धांतों में था और सीधे न्यायालय में प्रवर्तनीय मौलिक अधिकार नहीं था। 86वें संविधान संशोधन, 2002 ने अनुच्छेद 45 का विषय प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखरेख और छह वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों की शिक्षा पर केंद्रित कर दिया तथा अनुच्छेद 21क जोड़ा।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Article 45

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The original text of Article 45 in the 1950 Constitution set a ten-year time frame for the State to provide free and compulsory education for all children until fourteen years of age. This non-justiciable directive remained until replaced by the 86th Amendment Act in 2002.

questions.question_english: Read the situation below and answer the question that follows: A local authority issues an order making it mandatory for all schools in the district, including linguistic minority schools, to teach the local state language as the primary medium of instruction. questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the constitutional validity of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009:
I. It was challenged on the ground that it violates the fundamental right of private school managements under Article 19(1)(g).
II. The Supreme Court held that the RTE Act is constitutionally valid and its provisions constitute reasonable restrictions in the interest of the general public.

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the role of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) in education:
I. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act added the Eleventh Schedule, which includes 'Education, including primary and secondary schools'.
II. PRIs have exclusive legislative power over primary education, overriding state laws.
III. The transfer of primary education management to PRIs is a constitutional mandate but its actual devolution depends on State legislatures. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation_english: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act added the 11th Schedule, entry 17 of which includes primary and secondary education. Devolution of administrative control over primary schools to PRIs is subject to legislation by State Legislatures. Statement II is incorrect as PRIs do not hold exclusive overriding legislative powers over States.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I और III। 73वें संविधान संशोधन ने ग्यारहवीं अनुसूची जोड़ी; इसकी प्रविष्टि 17 में प्राथमिक और माध्यमिक शिक्षा शामिल है। यह पंचायतों के संभावित कार्यक्षेत्र को संवैधानिक आधार प्रदान करती है। परंतु पंचायतों को राज्य विधानमंडल से ऊपर या राज्य कानूनों को निरस्त करने वाली अनन्य विधायी शक्ति नहीं मिलती। प्रशासनिक और वित्तीय जिम्मेदारियों का वास्तविक हस्तांतरण संबंधित राज्य कानूनों और व्यवस्था पर निर्भर करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act added the 11th Schedule, entry 17 of which includes primary and secondary education. Devolution of administrative control over primary schools to PRIs is subject to legislation by State Legislatures. questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: वैज्ञानिक दृष्टिकोण, मानववाद तथा जाँच-पड़ताल और सुधार की भावना विकसित करना। अनुच्छेद 51क(ज) प्रत्येक नागरिक का कर्तव्य बताता है कि वह वैज्ञानिक दृष्टिकोण, मानववाद तथा जाँच-पड़ताल और सुधार की भावना विकसित करे। विद्यालय में प्रमाण-आधारित सोच, प्रश्न पूछना, प्रयोग करना और तर्कपूर्ण निष्कर्ष निकालना इस कर्तव्य को व्यावहारिक रूप से प्रोत्साहित कर सकते हैं। अन्य विकल्प भी मौलिक कर्तव्य हैं, लेकिन वे प्रश्न में वर्णित वैज्ञानिक चिंतन के सबसे सीधे संदर्भ नहीं हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 51A(h) explicitly states that it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform. This fundamental duty forms the constitutional foundation for promoting inquiry-based learning, science education, and critical thinking in school curricula.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): In India, a person cannot establish an educational institution purely for the motive of making a profit.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court has repeatedly held that education is treated as a charitable occupation, not a trade or business for profit under Article 19(1)(g).
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Supreme Court rulings in Unni Krishnan and TMA Pai established that while running an educational institution is an occupation under Article 19(1)(g), education is inherently a charitable activity. Commercialization and profiteering are strictly forbidden, making the reason a direct explanation of the assertion.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: A और R दोनों सही हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है। उन्नीकृष्णन और T.M.A. Pai सहित निर्णयों ने माना कि शैक्षणिक संस्था चलाना अनुच्छेद 19(1)(g) के अंतर्गत व्यवसाय/व्यवसायिक गतिविधि के रूप में संरक्षित हो सकता है, लेकिन शिक्षा को मात्र लाभ कमाने का साधन नहीं बनाया जा सकता। संस्थान उचित अधिशेष रख सकता है, पर मुनाफाखोरी और कैपिटेशन फीस स्वीकार्य नहीं हैं। इसीलिए कारण, अभिकथन के पीछे कानूनी सिद्धांत स्पष्ट करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Supreme Court rulings in Unni Krishnan and TMA Pai established that while running an educational institution is an occupation under Article 19(1)(g), education is inherently a charitable activity. Commercialization and profiteering are strictly forbidden, making the reason a direct explanation of the assertion.

questions.question_hindi:
विद्यालयों में समानता के अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 14) के प्रयोग के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. यह सरकारी सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालयों द्वारा मनमाने शुल्क-वृद्धि जैसे निर्णयों पर रोक लगाने का आधार बन सकता है।
II. यह अपेक्षा करता है कि शारीरिक दिव्यांगता वाले विद्यार्थियों को बिना किसी विशेष सुविधा के हर दूसरे विद्यार्थी की बिल्कुल समान पद्धति से शिक्षा दी जाए।
III. यह समावेशी शिक्षा के लिए उचित सुविधाएँ और समायोजन उपलब्ध कराने की नीति का आधार बनता है।
कौन-से कथन सही हैं?

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the application of Article 14 (Right to Equality) in schools:
I. It prohibits arbitrary fee hikes by government-aided schools.
II. It requires that all students, regardless of physical disabilities, must be taught in the exact same manner without any special accommodations.
III. It forms the basis for inclusive education policies, ensuring reasonable accommodations are provided to level the playing field. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation_english: Article 14 prevents arbitrary administrative decisions like unreasonable fee hikes and demands reasonable classification for disadvantaged groups, forming the foundation of inclusive education. Statement II is incorrect because treating disabled students identically without reasonable accommodations fails equal protection by ignoring relevant functional differences.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I और III। अनुच्छेद 14 मनमाने राज्यीय कार्यों पर रोक और समान संरक्षण का आधार प्रदान करता है। विद्यालयों में यह नियमों की तर्कसंगतता और समानता की अपेक्षा से जुड़ सकता है। दूसरा कथन गलत है: समानता का अर्थ सभी को बिल्कुल एक जैसा व्यवहार देना नहीं होता, विशेषकर जब विद्यार्थियों को सार्थक भागीदारी के लिए उचित सुविधाओं या समायोजन की आवश्यकता हो। समावेशी शिक्षा बाधाओं को दूर करके वास्तविक समान अवसर सुनिश्चित करने का प्रयास करती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 14 prevents arbitrary administrative decisions like unreasonable fee hikes and demands reasonable classification for disadvantaged groups, forming the foundation of inclusive education. Statement II is incorrect because treating disabled students identically without reasonable accommodations fails equal protection by ignoring relevant functional differences.

questions.question_english: Which Article of the Constitution empowers the President to appoint a Commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes, which historically impacted reservation policies in educational institutions?
questions.explanation_english: Article 340 empowers the President to appoint a Commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes. Historical bodies like the Kaka Kalelkar Commission and Mandal Commission were constituted under Article 340, shaping backward class identification for affirmative action in education.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: अनुच्छेद 340। यह राष्ट्रपति को सामाजिक और शैक्षणिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्गों की दशा, कठिनाइयों और उन्नति के लिए आवश्यक कदमों की जाँच करने हेतु आयोग नियुक्त करने का अधिकार देता है। काका कालेलकर आयोग और मंडल आयोग जैसे ऐतिहासिक आयोग इस संवैधानिक व्यवस्था से संबंधित रहे। अनुच्छेद 341 अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुच्छेद 342 अनुसूचित जनजातियों की अधिसूचना से संबंधित है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 338 राष्ट्रीय अनुसूचित जाति आयोग से जुड़ा है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Article 340

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 340 empowers the President to appoint a Commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes. Historical bodies like the Kaka Kalelkar Commission and Mandal Commission were constituted under Article 340, shaping backward class identification for affirmative action in education.

questions.question_hindi: दिल्ली के एक सरकारी विद्यालय की स्कूल प्रबंधन समिति विद्यालय के खेल मैदान पर स्थायी मंदिर बनाने के लिए विद्यालय निधि का उपयोग करने का प्रस्ताव पारित करती है। प्रधानाचार्य की सबसे उपयुक्त संवैधानिक और प्रशासनिक प्रतिक्रिया क्या होगी?

निर्माण की अनुमति तभी देना जब स्थानीय विधायक निधि से भवन की लागत चुकाई जाए।

questions.question_english: A school management committee (SMC) in a Delhi government school resolves to utilize school funds to build a permanent temple on the school playground. As a Principal, what is the most constitutionally sound administrative response?
options_english: Allow the proposal unconditionally, as the School Management Committee possesses statutory administrative autonomy.
Disallow it under Article 28(1) due to the secular nature of state institutions.
Allow the proposal conditionally, provided that parents representing all other religious faiths raise no formal objections.
Disallow the construction proposal, unless local constituency development funds explicitly finance the building costs.
questions.explanation_english: Article 28(1) prohibits religious instruction or the establishment of permanent religious structures within educational institutions wholly maintained out of State funds. key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Disallow it under Article 28(1) due to the secular nature of state institutions.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 28(1) prohibits religious instruction or the establishment of permanent religious structures within educational institutions wholly maintained out of State funds. Constructing a permanent religious site on government school land violates the state's secular mandate, making it obligatory for the Principal to reject the proposal.

II. पृथक्करणीयता का सिद्धांत: किसी कानून के असंवैधानिक हिस्से को हटाकर शेष कानून को बनाए रखना।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following pairs of legal doctrines and their application to educational constitutional law:
I. Doctrine of Basic Structure: Applied in cases to argue that the Right to Education is essential to a dignified life.
II. Doctrine of Severability: Used to strike down unconstitutional parts of educational statutes while keeping the rest intact.
III. Doctrine of Repugnancy: Relevant when a State Education Act conflicts with a Central Education Act. Which pairs above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation_english: All three matches are legally accurate. Basic Structure applies to core rights including education; Severability isolates unconstitutional statutory clauses without invalidating entire Acts; and Repugnancy under Article 254 resolves operational conflicts between State and Central education legislation.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) I, II and III

questions.question_hindi:
स्थिति पर विचार कीजिए।
केंद्र सरकार समग्र शिक्षा योजना शुरू करती है, जिसमें सर्व शिक्षा अभियान, RMSA और शिक्षक शिक्षा को समाहित किया गया है। योजना के लिए राज्यों को 40 प्रतिशत धन देना है। एक राज्य इसे अपनी स्वायत्तता में हस्तक्षेप बताते हुए मना कर देता है। शिक्षा के समवर्ती-सूची ढाँचे में ऐसी केंद्र प्रायोजित योजनाओं को संवैधानिक आधार किस प्रावधान से मिल सकता है?
options_hindi: अनुच्छेद 248 के अंतर्गत संसद की अनन्य अवशिष्ट विधायी शक्ति का सीधे उपयोग करके।
सार्वजनिक प्रयोजनों के लिए अनुदान देने की अनुच्छेद 282 की शक्ति का उपयोग करके।
अनुच्छेद 360 के अंतर्गत राष्ट्रीय वित्तीय आपातकाल घोषित करके।
संघ सूची की प्रविष्टि 66 के अंतर्गत उच्च शिक्षा के मानकों पर केंद्रीय विधायी अधिकार का उपयोग करके।

questions.question_english: Read the situation below and answer the question that follows: The Union Government launches the Samagra Shiksha scheme, subsuming SSA, RMSA, and TE. The scheme requires states to contribute 40% of the funds. A state refuses, citing it as an infringement on its autonomy. Under the Concurrent List framework, how are such Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) constitutionally justified in education?
options_english: By directly invoking the exclusive residuary legislative powers vested in the Parliament of India under Article 248.
By utilizing Article 282 to make grants for public financial purposes.
By issuing formal constitutional proclamations declaring a nationwide financial emergency under Article 360.
By exercising the Union's legislative authority over higher education standards under Entry 66 of List I.
questions.explanation_english: Article 282 empowers the Union or a State to make financial grants for any public purpose, even if outside their direct legislative domain. Centrally Sponsored Schemes like Samagra Shiksha are legally structured and funded under Article 282 grants, facilitating shared Centre-State financial participation in educational development.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: अनुच्छेद 282। यह संघ या राज्य को किसी सार्वजनिक प्रयोजन के लिए अनुदान देने की अनुमति देता है, भले ही वह प्रयोजन उनके प्रत्यक्ष विधायी क्षेत्र से बाहर हो। समग्र शिक्षा जैसी केंद्र प्रायोजित योजनाओं में वित्तीय सहायता तथा केंद्र-राज्य हिस्सेदारी की व्यवस्था इस तरह के सार्वजनिक-वित्तीय प्रावधानों से जुड़ सकती है। अनुच्छेद 248 अवशिष्ट विधायी शक्ति, अनुच्छेद 360 वित्तीय आपातकाल और संघ सूची की प्रविष्टि 66 उच्च शिक्षा के मानकों के समन्वय तथा निर्धारण से संबंधित है; ये दिए गए प्रसंग का सबसे सीधा आधार नहीं हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) By utilizing Article 282 to make grants for public financial purposes.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 282 empowers the Union or a State to make financial grants for any public purpose, even if outside their direct legislative domain. Centrally Sponsored Schemes like Samagra Shiksha are legally structured and funded under Article 282 grants, facilitating shared Centre-State financial participation in educational development.

questions.question_english: Which one of the following Constitutional Amendments gave constitutional status and protection to cooperative societies, adding Article 43B, a principle of democratic control often mirrored in the functioning of Parent-Teacher Associations and SMCs?
questions.explanation_english: The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 added Article 43B to the Directive Principles, encouraging the voluntary formation and democratic control of co-operative societies. This principle of participatory democratic management mirrors community-led governance structures like Parent-Teacher Associations and School Management Committees under educational frameworks.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: 97वाँ संविधान संशोधन। 2011 के 97वें संशोधन ने राज्य नीति के निदेशक सिद्धांतों में अनुच्छेद 43ख जोड़ा, जिसमें सहकारी समितियों के स्वैच्छिक गठन, स्वायत्त कार्य और लोकतांत्रिक नियंत्रण को प्रोत्साहित करने की बात है। प्रश्न इस सिद्धांत को सहभागी संस्थागत प्रबंधन से जोड़ता है। हालांकि सहकारी समितियों और स्कूल प्रबंधन समितियों की कानूनी प्रकृति अलग है, लोकतांत्रिक भागीदारी और पारदर्शी निर्णय-प्रक्रिया दोनों में महत्त्वपूर्ण हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) 97th Amendment

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 added Article 43B to the Directive Principles, encouraging the voluntary formation and democratic control of co-operative societies. questions.question_hindi:
शिक्षा के अधिकार और बाल श्रम के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. अनुच्छेद 24 चौदह वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों को कारखानों या जोखिमपूर्ण रोजगार में लगाने पर रोक लगाता है।
II. बाल श्रम (निषेध और विनियमन) संशोधन अधिनियम, 2016 ने चौदह वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों के रोजगार पर प्रतिबंध लगाकर कानून को RTE अधिनियम के साथ समन्वित किया, हालांकि विद्यालय समय के बाद पारिवारिक उद्यमों में सीमित अपवाद रखे गए।
III. संविधान स्पष्ट रूप से कहता है कि काम करने वाले बच्चे औपचारिक शिक्षा प्राप्त नहीं कर सकते।
कौन-से कथन सही हैं?

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the Right to Education and child labor:
I. Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in factories or hazardous employment.
II. The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016 completely aligned the child labor laws with the RTE Act by prohibiting all employment of children below 14 years, with limited exceptions for family enterprises after school hours.
III. The Constitution explicitly states that working children cannot access formal education. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation_english: Article 24 forbids hazardous child labor under fourteen, and the 2016 Child Labour Amendment aligned rules with the RTE Act by enacting a complete ban on child employment under 14 years. Statement III is incorrect as the Constitution does not exclude working children from formal educational rights.
questions.explanation_hindi: स्रोत के अनुसार सही उत्तर है: I और II। अनुच्छेद 24 चौदह वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों को कारखानों, खानों और जोखिमपूर्ण रोजगार में लगाए जाने से सुरक्षा देता है। 2016 के बाल श्रम संशोधन ने चौदह वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों के काम के संबंध में व्यापक निषेध स्थापित किया, जिसमें कानून में बताए गए सीमित अपवाद भी शामिल हैं। तीसरा कथन गलत है: संविधान यह नहीं कहता कि काम करने वाला बच्चा औपचारिक शिक्षा से वंचित ही रहेगा; इसके विपरीत, बाल श्रम पर रोक और शिक्षा का अधिकार परस्पर पूरक हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 24 forbids hazardous child labor under fourteen, and the 2016 Child Labour Amendment aligned rules with the RTE Act by enacting a complete ban on child employment under 14 years. Statement III is incorrect as the Constitution does not exclude working children from formal educational rights.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Right to Information (RTI) Act is heavily utilized by parents to access school records and admission criteria.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court has held that the right to information is implicitly guaranteed by Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of speech and expression) of the Constitution.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: The Supreme Court held in State of UP v. Raj Narain and subsequent cases that the right to know and access public information is derived from freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a). The RTI Act operationalizes this fundamental right, making the reason a direct explanation.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: A और R दोनों सही हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने राज्य से संबंधित मामलों में जानने और सार्वजनिक सूचना तक पहुँच के अधिकार को अनुच्छेद 19(1)(क) की वाक् और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता से जोड़ा है। इसी संवैधानिक पृष्ठभूमि में सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 सार्वजनिक प्राधिकरणों से जानकारी प्राप्त करने की प्रक्रिया निर्धारित करता है। अभिभावक प्रवेश मानदंड, शुल्क, विद्यालयी रिकॉर्ड और प्रशासनिक निर्णयों की जानकारी के लिए इसका उपयोग कर सकते हैं, लागू अपवादों के अधीन।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Supreme Court held in State of UP v. Raj Narain and subsequent cases that the right to know and access public information is derived from freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a). The RTI Act operationalizes this fundamental right, making the reason a direct explanation.

questions.question_english: A student is subjected to corporal punishment in a government school resulting in physical injury. Besides the RTE Act and IPC, which Fundamental Right is directly violated?
questions.explanation_english: Physical punishment causing harm directly infringes the fundamental right to live with human dignity and personal liberty under Article 21. Judicial decisions explicitly state that subjecting children to violent disciplinary measures violates physical integrity and personal security guaranteed by Article 21 of the Constitution.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: अनुच्छेद 21। जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार केवल जीवित रहने तक सीमित नहीं है; इसमें गरिमा और शारीरिक अखंडता की सुरक्षा भी शामिल है। विद्यालय में ऐसा शारीरिक दंड जिससे चोट, अपमान या मानसिक आघात हो, बच्चे की गरिमा के विरुद्ध हो सकता है। इसके अतिरिक्त RTE अधिनियम की धारा 17 शारीरिक दंड और मानसिक उत्पीड़न पर रोक लगाती है; संबंधित तथ्य के आधार पर अन्य कानूनी प्रावधान भी लागू हो सकते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Article 21

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Physical punishment causing harm directly infringes the fundamental right to live with human dignity and personal liberty under Article 21. Judicial decisions explicitly state that subjecting children to violent disciplinary measures violates physical integrity and personal security guaranteed by Article 21 of the Constitution.

शैक्षणिक कानून बनाने में राष्ट्रपति/उपराज्यपाल की भूमिका से संबंधित निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. दिल्ली विधानसभा द्वारा पारित विद्यालयी शिक्षा संबंधी विधेयक के लिए उपराज्यपाल की संवैधानिक प्रक्रिया के अनुसार स्वीकृति आवश्यक होती है।
II. यदि उपराज्यपाल विधेयक राष्ट्रपति के विचारार्थ आरक्षित करे और राष्ट्रपति स्वीकृति दे दे, तो समवर्ती सूची के विषय पर दिल्ली का कानून पहले के विरोधी संसदीय कानून पर दिल्ली में प्रभावी हो सकता है।
III. राष्ट्रपति कार्यपालिका के आदेश से सभी राज्य बोर्ड विद्यालय बंद करने का निर्देश दे सकता है।

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the role of the President/Governor in educational legislation:
I. A Bill passed by the Delhi Legislative Assembly regarding school education requires the assent of the Lieutenant Governor.
II. If the LG reserves the Bill for the consideration of the President, and the President assents to it, the Delhi law will prevail in Delhi even if it is repugnant to an earlier Parliamentary law on the same subject in the Concurrent List.
III. The President can mandate the closure of all state board schools via an executive order. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation_english: Bills passed by the Delhi Legislative Assembly require LG assent under Article 239AA. If reserved for the President and assented to, the state law prevails over prior conflicting Central law under Article 254(2). Statement III is incorrect as the President cannot arbitrarily close state schools by executive order.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I और II। अनुच्छेद 239कक के अंतर्गत दिल्ली की विधायी प्रक्रिया में उपराज्यपाल की संवैधानिक भूमिका है। अनुच्छेद 254(2) के तहत, यदि समवर्ती सूची के विषय पर दिल्ली का विधेयक राष्ट्रपति के विचारार्थ आरक्षित हो और राष्ट्रपति की स्वीकृति प्राप्त करे, तो वह उस क्षेत्र में पहले के केंद्रीय कानून से असंगत होने पर भी प्रभावी हो सकता है, जब तक संसद बाद में उसे बदल न दे। तीसरा कथन गलत है, क्योंकि राष्ट्रपति के पास बिना विधिक आधार सभी राज्य बोर्ड विद्यालयों को बंद करने की सामान्य कार्यपालिका शक्ति नहीं है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Bills passed by the Delhi Legislative Assembly require LG assent under Article 239AA. If reserved for the President and assented to, the state law prevails over prior conflicting Central law under Article 254(2). Statement III is incorrect as the President cannot arbitrarily close state schools by executive order.

questions.question_english: In the context of constitutional law, an educational institution established by a registered society consisting entirely of members of a religious minority community, but functioning completely on a secular basis without promoting that religion, is:
options_english: Entitled to minority status based on its establishment by the minority community.
Completely disqualified from claiming minority status guarantees enshrined under Article 30(1).
Legally required to surrender its constitutional minority status to obtain official state recognition.
Categorized and treated as a standard non-minority majority institution by administrative default.
questions.explanation_english: Article 30(1) grants minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions. Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 311(2) mandates that no civil servant (including government teachers holding civil posts) shall be dismissed, removed, or reduced in rank except after an inquiry informing them of charges and giving a reasonable opportunity to be heard. key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) No, appointment of public servants is governed by statutory rules under Article 309.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Public school principals and teachers are civil posts governed by recruitment rules framed under Article 309. Parents or School Management Committees do not possess constitutional or statutory selection authority to directly hire public servants, as public appointment processes must adhere strictly to statutory service rules.

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019:
I. It extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.

questions.explanation_english: The 104th Amendment Act extended reservation for SCs and STs in Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for ten years while terminating nominated Anglo-Indian representation. Statements I and III are correct, but II is incorrect because it discontinued, rather than extended, reserved seats for Anglo-Indians.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I और III। 104वें संशोधन ने लोकसभा और राज्य विधानसभाओं में अनुसूचित जातियों तथा अनुसूचित जनजातियों के लिए सीट आरक्षण की अवधि बढ़ाई, जबकि आंग्ल-भारतीय समुदाय के नामित प्रतिनिधित्व की व्यवस्था समाप्त कर दी। इसलिए दूसरा कथन गलत है। शिक्षा में आरक्षण पर यह संशोधन सीधे नए शैक्षणिक कोटे का प्रावधान नहीं करता, पर सकारात्मक कार्रवाई के संवैधानिक संदर्भ से इसका अप्रत्यक्ष संबंध है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The 104th Amendment Act extended reservation for SCs and STs in Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for ten years while terminating nominated Anglo-Indian representation. Statements I and III are correct, but II is incorrect because it discontinued, rather than extended, reserved seats for Anglo-Indians.

questions.question_hindi: स्थिति पर विचार कीजिए। दृष्टिबाधित विद्यार्थियों का एक समूह उच्च न्यायालय में याचिका दायर करता है कि सरकारी विद्यालयों में ब्रेल पुस्तकें और सुलभ शौचालय उपलब्ध नहीं हैं, जिससे उनके शिक्षा के अधिकार का उल्लंघन होता है। राज्य सरकार को सुधारात्मक आदेश देने के लिए उच्च न्यायालय किस प्रावधान के अंतर्गत रिट जारी कर सकता है?
